record.paper_title: Kinetic plasma turbulence: recent insights and open questions from 3D3V simulations
record.original_question: What are the high-order statistics of fluctuations in kinetic plasma turbulence? In context, this means determining the intermittency-sensitive, non-Gaussian statistical structure of the turbulent fields at kinetic scales, beyond low-order spectral descriptions.

evidence.quote: This includes answering fundamental questions about, for instance, ... (iii) the high-order statistics of the fluctuations

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a fully ionized, weakly collisional, magnetized plasma in three spatial and three velocity dimensions, modeled by the Vlasov–Maxwell system

  ∂_t f_s + v·∇_x f_s + (q_s/m_s)(E + v×B/c)·∇_v f_s = 0,   s = i, e,
  ∂_t B = −c∇×E,    ∇×B = (4π/c) Σ_s q_s ∫ v f_s d^3v + (1/c) ∂_t E,
  ∇·B = 0,    ∇·E = 4π Σ_s q_s ∫ f_s d^3v,

driven into a statistically steady, strongly turbulent state with a mean magnetic field B_0 and characteristic ion gyroradius ρ_i and inertial length d_i. Let δψ_ℓ(x) = ψ(x+ℓ) − ψ(x) denote the spatial increment of a fluctuating field ψ ∈ {B, E, u_s, n_s, …} over a separation ℓ, and define the structure functions

  S_p^ψ(ℓ) = ⟨ |δψ_ℓ|^p ⟩,    p ≥ 1,

together with the scale-dependent kurtosis

  K^ψ(ℓ) = S_4^ψ(ℓ) / [S_2^ψ(ℓ)]^2,

and the standardized probability density functions P(δψ_ℓ / σ_ℓ).

Determine the high-order statistical structure of the turbulent fluctuations across the kinetic range ℓ ≲ ρ_i, d_i. Specifically:

(a) Characterize, for each field ψ, the scaling exponents ζ_p^ψ defined by S_p^ψ(ℓ) ∼ ℓ^{ζ_p^ψ} and the resulting multifractal spectrum, including any departure from a linear (self-similar) dependence ζ_p^ψ = p·ζ_1^ψ.

(b) Determine the scale dependence of K^ψ(ℓ) and of the full PDF P(δψ_ℓ/σ_ℓ) at sub-ion scales, including whether intermittency increases, saturates, or decreases as ℓ crosses ρ_i and d_i down to electron scales.

(c) Identify which fields (magnetic field components, electric field, ion and electron bulk velocities, densities) display the strongest non-Gaussian, intermittent behavior, and relate the observed higher-order statistics to the coherent structures (current sheets, vortices, reconnection sites) that produce them.
artifact.status_search_result: The high-order statistical structure of fluctuations at kinetic (sub-ion to electron) scales in collisionless plasma turbulence remains an active and unresolved area. Recent observational and numerical studies (MMS observations, 3D3V Vlasov simulations, hybrid PIC, HelioSwarm forecasts) report partial and sometimes conflicting results: some find a transition from intermittent to globally self-similar non-Gaussian statistics below ρ_i, while others report sustained intermittency tied to current sheets and reconnection, and electron-scale statistics are still poorly constrained. No complete theory of the multifractal spectrum and PDFs across the kinetic range exists.

status_evidence.title: Spectral anisotropies and intermittency of plasma turbulence at ion kinetic scales
status_evidence.snippet: Higher-order statistics show that both parallel and perpendicular fluctuations are an isotropic globally scale-invariant non-Gaussian process at sub-ion scales.
status_evidence.claim: Findings on sub-ion intermittency are still being characterized and debated.

status_evidence.title: Higher-Order Statistics in Compressive Solar Wind Plasma Turbulence (MMS)
status_evidence.snippet: PDFs become non-Gaussian with sharper peaks and thicker tails as scale decreases into the kinetic range.
status_evidence.claim: Scale-dependent non-Gaussianity at kinetic scales is observationally documented but not fully explained.

status_evidence.title: Evaluation of Scale-dependent Kurtosis with HelioSwarm
status_evidence.snippet: Future multi-spacecraft missions are designed to better measure scale-dependent kurtosis at kinetic scales.
status_evidence.claim: Open question being addressed by upcoming missions, indicating it is not resolved.

status_evidence.title: Machine-Learning Characterization of Intermittency in Relativistic Pair Plasma Turbulence
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024–2025) studies continue to characterize intermittent coherent structures in kinetic plasma turbulence.
status_evidence.claim: Active ongoing research on identifying intermittent structures in kinetic plasma turbulence.
